t.6.82.1: Those thousands of elephants, and horses with their riders, and chariots by the thousands, bright as fire and bearing banners,
t.6.82.2: Thousands of rākṣasas, warriors fighting with maces and iron bars, splendid with golden banners, heroic and able to take any form at will.
t.6.82.4: Having seen and heard this, the night-roamers who survived the slaughter were bewildered, and the rākṣasīs too, gathering together, were wretched and overwhelmed with anxiety.
t.6.82.3: Those sent forth by Rāvaṇa were struck down by Rāma, tireless in his deeds, with sharp arrows adorned with refined gold.
t.6.82.5: The rākṣasīs, widowed, their sons slain and their kinsmen killed, crying out and stricken with grief, gathered together and lamented.
t.6.82.6: How did Śūrpaṇakhā, old, hideous and pot-bellied, approach Rāma in the forest, who was like Kandarpa himself in bodily form?
t.6.82.7: Seeing him, tender and of great spirit, devoted to the welfare of all beings, she, ugly of form and deserving death at the hands of the world, was filled with desire.
t.6.82.8: How did the ugly-faced rākṣasī, devoid of all virtues, come to desire Rāma, the virtuous one of great vigor and handsome face?
t.6.82.9: Through the ill fortune of this people, that wrinkled old woman with white hair committed a deed that was improper, laughable, and condemned by all the world.
t.6.82.10: To the ruin of the rākṣasas, and of Dūṣaṇa and Khara, that ill-favoured woman made her assault upon Rāghava.
t.6.82.12: And yet Daśagrīva does not obtain Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, while an undying enmity has been bound with the mighty Rāghava.
t.6.82.11: It was for her sake that Rāvaṇa created this great enmity, and that same Sītā has been led to her death by the ten-necked rākṣasa.
t.6.82.13: Having seen that rākṣasa Virādha, who sought Vaidehī, slain by Rāma alone, that example is sufficient proof.
t.6.82.14: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds were slain in Janasthāna by arrows resembling tongues of fire.
t.6.82.15: Khara was slain in battle, and likewise Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras, by arrows resembling the sun; that is example enough.
t.6.82.17: Rāma slew the mighty Vālin, son of the thousand-eyed one, who resembled a cloud; that is example enough.
t.6.82.16: Kabandha too, the blood-eater whose arms stretched a yojana, was slain as he roared, tormented by rage; that alone is proof enough.
t.6.82.18: Sugrīva, who was living wretched on Mount Ṛśyamūka with his hopes shattered, was established in the kingship; that is sufficient proof of it.
t.6.82.19: The fitting counsel spoken by Vibhīṣaṇa, joined with righteousness and profit and beneficial to all the rākṣasas, does not please him because of his delusion.
t.6.82.20: If the younger brother of Dhanada had followed the words of Vibhīṣaṇa, this city of Laṅkā would not have become a cremation ground, stricken with sorrow.
t.6.82.21: Though he has heard that the mighty Kumbhakarṇa was slain by Rāghava, and his dear son Indrajit as well, Rāvaṇa still does not come to his senses.
t.6.82.22: "My son, my brother, my husband has been slain in battle!" Such is the cry that is heard in house after house of the Rākṣasas.
t.6.82.23: Chariots, horses and elephants were slain by the hundred thousands in battle by the heroic Rāma, and so too were the Rākṣasas fighting on foot.
t.6.82.24: Whether it be Rudra, or Viṣṇu, or great Indra of a hundred sacrifices, or even Antaka himself, it is he who slays us in the form of Rāma.
t.6.82.25: Our foremost heroes slain by Rāma, we, hopeless of life, seeing no end to our fear, lament without a protector.
t.6.82.26: Daśagrīva, valiant in battle and endowed with boons, does not perceive this most dreadful danger that has arisen from the hand of Rāma.
t.6.82.27: Neither the gods nor the Gandharvas, neither the Piśācas nor the Rākṣasas are able to save one who has been assailed by Rāma in battle.
t.6.82.28: Ill omens, too, are seen for Rāvaṇa in battle after battle; they will proclaim the slaying of Rāvaṇa by Rāma.
t.6.82.30: This, I think, is beyond all doubt the terrible danger that has come from a human being, one that will bring an end to the lives of the rākṣasas and of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.82.29: The pleased Grandfather granted Rāvaṇa freedom from fear at the hands of the Devas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, but protection from humans was not asked for.
t.6.82.31: Oppressed by the mighty rākṣasa through the granting of a boon, the gods worshipped Pitāmaha with blazing austerities.
t.6.82.32: For the welfare of the gods, the great-souled Grandfather, being pleased, spoke these momentous words to all the deities.
t.6.82.33: From this day forth, all the Dānavas and Rākṣasas, ever enveloped by fear, shall wander the three worlds forevermore.
t.6.82.34: Then all the deities, with Indra at their head, came together and propitiated Mahādeva, the destroyer of Tripura, whose banner bears the bull.
t.6.82.35: But Mahādeva, pleased, spoke these words to the gods: "For your welfare a woman will be born who will bring about the destruction of the Rākṣasas."
t.6.82.36: This Sītā, sent forth by the gods, is a destroyer of rākṣasas. Like the hunger that once devoured the Dānavas, she will devour us together with Rāvaṇa.
t.6.82.37: Because of the misconduct of Rāvaṇa, the ill-disciplined and evil-minded, this dreadful wailing has arisen, overflowing with grief.
t.6.82.38: We see no one in the world who could give us refuge, assailed as we are by Rāghava, as if by Kāla at the end of a yuga.
t.6.82.39: Thus lamenting, all the wives of the night-roaming Rākṣasas embraced one another with their arms and sank down in despair, afflicted and tormented by extreme fear, and then they wailed aloud most terribly.
